findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts are strongest and most reproducible for pair-distance shell densities at short separations: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive fraction 0.0). Branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations agree in sign and batch direction for 1.5 and 2.5 A shells. These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a standardized coordinate observable, not absolute geometric quality or interaction energies.

Shape-moment contrasts are negative and reproducible for shape_yy (integrated z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and shape_xx (-0.495, q 8.1e-4), with shape_yz also negative (-0.212, q 0.035) and shape_zz weaker (-0.183, q 0.067). The branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations for shape_yy are negative with same-sign batch fraction 1.0. Sign is defined only relative to the declared favorable-minus-comparison label; it is not a shared quality axis across observables.

Landmark softmin and occupancy contrasts are mixed in sign across regions: landmark_00_softmin is negative (-0.481, q 8.1e-4) while landmark_00_occupancy3 is positive (0.545, q 2.4e-4); landmark_02_softmin positive (0.253) with landmark_02_occupancy5 negative (-0.323); landmark_05_softmin positive (0.396) with landmark_05_occupancy5 negative (-0.344); landmark_06_softmin positive (0.294) with landmark_06_occupancy5 negative (-0.365); landmark_18_softmin positive (0.264) with landmark_18_occupancy5 negative (-0.311). Softmin (lower = closer) and occupancy (radial shell density, non-monotone in distance) are different observables, so opposite signs are not contradictory but also do not define a single favorable direction.

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity. Survival enrichment is positive for landmark_00_soft_mass (0.365, q 0.120), landmark_04_local_czz (0.266, q 0.302), landmark_07_soft_mass (0.220, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (0.234, q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz (0.217, q 0.302), and negative for several local_czz and local_cyy fields (e.g. landmark_05_local_czz -0.419, landmark_15_local_czz -0.399, landmark_09_local_czz -0.390, landmark_16_local_cyy -0.317). Because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, these cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Parent-child increment contrasts partly disagree with whole-window endpoint contrasts. landmark_00_softmin increment rate is negative (-4.91, q 0.046) consistent with its negative endpoint contrast, and landmark_00_occupancy3 increment is positive (4.28, q 0.081) consistent with its positive endpoint contrast; but shape_xx (-3.70, q 0.095) and shape_yy (-3.85, q 0.161) increments are negative while pair_kernel_2.5 increment is positive (3.96, q 0.208) and pair_kernel_7.0 negative (-3.14, q 0.208). Disagreement between immediate selection evidence and descendant credit affects direction priority and is not resolved by the supplied evidence.

Turnover accounting separates population-contrast change from parent-child increment contrasts. For several fields the edge (parent-child) rate and the turnover residual are large and opposite in sign to the population rate, e.g. landmark_00_local_cxx population -0.058 with edge -4.34 and residual +4.29; landmark_01_local_cyy population +1.03 with edge -5.37 and residual +6.40; landmark_16_local_cyy population +0.46 with edge -5.90 and residual +6.37. The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.

Supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolations over the complete observed window [0.0,0.49] with extrapolation disallowed and polynomial fits rejected. Many fields show multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts (e.g. landmark_00_local_dz 10 sign changes, 7 strong conflicts; landmark_01_local_cxy 7 sign changes, 18 conflicts; landmark_02_local_cyx-family 7-9 sign changes with 7-19 conflicts; landmark_06_local_cxz 13 sign changes, 13 conflicts). First and last rate z-values frequently have opposite signs (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass first +9.27, last -10.00), so a constant rule and a time-conditioned rule are not equivalent, and the curves are contrasts rather than absolute reward targets.

Curve-fidelity audit selects 24 of the supplied curves under the rule relative_node_rmse <= 0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes == 0, quiet_node_large_fit_fraction <= 0.1, absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857 and q < 0.05. The selected set includes pair_kernel_1.5, pair_kernel_2.5, shape_xx and shape_yy, but the audit also reports last empirical z and last fit z of opposite sign for many entries (e.g. landmark_00_softmin empirical -0.146 vs fit -0.481; landmark_02_occupancy5 empirical +0.142 vs fit -0.323), so fit fidelity does not establish a stable late-window direction.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible branch-adjusted effects: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are negative in raw covariance (z -5.15e-5 and -5.00e-5, q 0.038 and 0.044) and in adjusted covariance (z -3.60e-5 and -3.42e-5, q 0.020 and 0.030), with same-sign batch fraction 0.93 in the adjusted case. Raw and adjusted correlations are also negative with same-sign fraction 1.0. These are global pose/shape diagnostics, not local coordinate information, and the adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence rather than a rigid-motion residual computed here.

After branch adjustment, pair_kernel_1.5 and pair_kernel_2.5 remain positive in both covariance (z 7.67e-7 and 1.14e-6, q 0.081 and 0.077) and correlation (0.101 and 0.084, q 0.019 and 0.046) with same-sign batch fraction 0.93, while pair_kernel_3.5 and pair_kernel_5.0 lose significance (q 0.53 and 0.45) and pair_kernel_7.0 is negative (-0.050, q 0.129). This supports short-range pair-shell coupling beyond common motion but does not establish a chemical mechanism.

Joint diagnostics show selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment (0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with teacher innovation-contrast alignment (0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), but negatively associated with observed child score gain (-0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). Teacher contrast is dominated by internal fraction (0.787) with translation 0.132 and rotation 0.081, and atom participation fraction 0.384. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal affinity effects.

The information audit reports compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS of 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092) and proper-rigid RMS of 0.529 A (CI 0.468-0.582), with top4 teacher overlap 0.470 and chosen teacher score correlation 0.102 (compressed) and 0.064 (full). Teacher modes are static last-learning-node forecasts (28 teachers, assignment RMS quantiles 0.446/0.863/1.050 A) with temperature_edits false. Lineage support covers 14 complete-survival batches with 700 total batch nodes and terminal metadata at score time 0.99, but decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

hypotheses.claim: A testable coordinate hypothesis is that short-range pair-shell density (pair_kernel_1.5-2.5) is a favorable-direction observable at the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window, with intended response an increase in the signed favorable-minus-comparison contrast, target origin the supplied endpoint pointcloud, spatial scale 1.5-2.5 A, and temporal scale the full observed window. A discriminating failure condition is a sign reversal or loss of batch agreement in the pair_kernel_1.5-2.5 contrast under independent batches, or a negative increment contrast for the same field.

A second testable hypothesis is that shape_yy (and to a lesser extent shape_xx) is a reproducible negative-direction shape observable, with intended response a decrease in the signed contrast, target origin the global shape moment, spatial scale global, and temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition is a positive branch-adjusted correlation with same-sign batch fraction above 0.5, or a positive increment contrast for shape_yy.

A third hypothesis is that landmark soft-mass and local_czz survival enrichment at landmarks 00, 04, 07, 10 and 18 is a descendant-credit signal distinct from endpoint contrast, with intended response an increase in recorded joint-head survival credit, target origin the terminal lineage table, and temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition is a decoded terminal label that reverses the sign, or a turnover residual that fully accounts for the enrichment as reclassification.

A fourth hypothesis is that a time-conditioned contrast rule is preferable to a constant rule for fields with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts, using only observed-node interpolation within [0.0,0.49] and no extrapolation. A discriminating failure condition is a field whose first and last rate z-values agree in sign and whose sign-change count is zero, for which a constant rule would be adequate.

A fifth hypothesis is that joint innovation and internal RMS are global pose/shape diagnostics that should retain freedom rather than be treated as local coordinate information, with intended response a reduction in joint internal RMS, target origin the joint-motion diagnostic, spatial scale global, and temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition is a local region whose adjusted covariance adds information beyond the joint diagnostic, which would justify local rather than global treatment.

A sixth hypothesis is that large opposite-sign edge and turnover-residual rates indicate changing cohort composition rather than within-path change for the affected fields, with intended response a decomposition of population change into within-path and composition components, target origin the turnover accounting table, and temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition is a field whose population, edge and residual rates share sign and magnitude, which would support within-path change instead.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling, and is an accounting diagnostic rather than a causal selection effect.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals computed here.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis is permitted.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
Signs on different observables are not comparable as a shared quality axis without their definitions.
Pair kernels, moments and occupancy are diagnostic coordinate observables, not bond labels, interaction energies or neural-module causation.
